COLLECTED = 3 (clients must match; partner was off-by-one)
DELIVERED = 4
global switch gating bookDelivery creation
db.bookDelivery is bound to the hyphenated book-delivery collection
the immediate-assignment path adds maxETA with NO fallback - a missing or non-numeric value is a silent no-op, so expectedDeliveryAt comes out equal to pickupTime rather than invalid
the pending path's || 30 fallback rescues null/undefined/empty maxETA but not a non-numeric string - the asymmetry with the immediate path is the point

the CODE default is off and the code window is 10; production overrides both from delivery-company.delivery-config {type:'driver-assignment'} with true / 15. If this literal ever changes, the CORE note about reading the DB document rather than the constant needs rechecking
dispatch is scheduled at pickupTime minus assignmentWindowMinutes - the same quantity the late-delivery grace measures from the other end
business day crosses midnight; every slot is stored under the STARTING date
single per-weekday resolver; iterating the flat timeSlots over-books every weekday
the one correct business-day window ([D 09:00, D+1 02:00]); feeds the paid guarantee
dispatch requires a STRICT isActive === true on an area - {$ne: false} is a different, wrong set
pickupTime is stored as a bare HH:mm wall clock, which wraps past midnight - it is not a timestamp
the pending path stores the same wrapping HH:mm clock
update-delay moves pickupTime and does NOT recompute expectedDeliveryAt, so the stored promise belongs to originalPickupTime
the midnight roll-forward: a pickup clock earlier than the booking means the next day (1,774 rows)
the zero-minute-promise check reads the clock the promise was actually built from
the real store-ready source is orderFlowEvents status 3, keyed by orderNumber === bookDelivery.bookId - NOT a bookDelivery.storeReadyAt field, which nothing writes

the surviving storeReadyAt locals here read order.completedAt / orderFlowEvents, never bookDelivery.storeReadyAt (0 of 82,414 rows) - if a bookDelivery read reappears, the net-of-kitchen-delay lie is back

patterns.regex: logger\.error\('Failed to track centralized flow event:', error\);\s*\n\s*throw error;
patterns.desc: trackOrderFlowEvent rethrows - an unwrapped await on a dispatch route 5xxs the request after the write committed and skips the driver notifications

comment-to-courier is open to ANY dashboard user - no role allow-list, deliberately. The only token-side guard is a NON-EMPTY roles claim, which is what keeps customer / store-user / driver / impersonation tokens (minted with no roles) out. If this ever becomes a membership test again, or degrades to a mere existence check, the CORE note is wrong
the fresh shoofi-admin-users re-read asserts current ENROLMENT, not role membership - a deleted or fully-stripped account loses access at once instead of at token expiry 180 min later
admin roles are an OR with no hierarchy - master does NOT imply admin, which is why any allow-list on an admin surface silently excludes master/senior/operator/editor

the הערות לשליח edit button is rendered with NO role condition - the card gates only impersonation/re-charge on isMaster. A permission restriction here therefore shows as a 403 at save time, never as a hidden button; read the server guard, not this component
the client already ships 403 copy for this endpoint, which is how a server-side role gate surfaces to the user
driver client copy of delivery status enum
the only mobile driver-picker posts to the company-admin reassign endpoint
twin pairs collapse into TwinOrderCard unless mode is split
partner delivery status must match server (fixed off-by-one)
